beat: An Owing correct at every step: four months for a boat, eleven years running (BC01)
The burnt Rose registers and estate ledgers as one class of document (BC02)
Ussa-Rekh's thirty years of forgiveness and the brokerage that now indentures the dock crews (BC03)
The procession of the Argonian dead carried home by name by Grave-Singer Ossu through contested crossings (BC05)
What the Rose Becomes, ending in a unglamorous reform of assessment itself (BC06)
Protected in every end: the archive wing, the confiscation-ledger record class and the Rose heirs as a community
Each quest is found by rumour, shrine, book or strange encounter, never a quest board
Each Prince's bargain or curse is literally true and quietly ruinous (door wishes, mask wants, drowned-library price)
The player makes a real choice about which side or hunt to finish (cure, quarantine, expose or let it run; which hunt)
At least one element in each stays unexplained (wonder budget)
Fixed unique artifact rewards, not scaled loot
Horror is found through hospitality, memory or rite rather than only through combat
Early cases are petty crimes: thefts and larcenies
Cases escalate in series of thefts, larcenies and murder mysteries as rank rises
Rivalry with the Shadowscales and the Night-Reed Chapter runs through the line
Recurring cast and a rival, with clues for the finale seeded along the way
Grand finale: a murder mystery that must involve highly important NPCs of Black Marsh
A resident is refused registration because no Hist claims them (LW01), and the lore remedy of the Hissmir trials sharpens rather than solves it
The murdered delegate who was exposing League financiers, with the hate-crime story that suits many groups (LW04)
The traditional ordeal demanded in a mixed court (LW05)
The canal that improves sanitation but cuts a sacred route and displaces households (LW08)
The charter negotiation where prior cases limit credible clauses (LW09)
The finale: plural civic movement, merchant oligarchy, municipal service, or collapse after exposing its own contradictions (LW10)
Every quest starts from a causal local situation (geography, culture, politics, someone's motive) rather than a fetch list.
No quest is only collecting objects; recovery needs ownership, route, danger or interpretation to make it a problem.
The quest-giver is the payload: a person with a local occupation and one stated want.
Each region packet holds at least one oddity with no faction stakes, reward or explanation.
Cross-line texture comes through shared places and networks, never imported characters; delivery stays mostly low-tier (moved evidence, aftermath, retrieval).

MQ01: the Owing-gang processing, then the Unbound Root's attack led in person by Cuts-the-Old-Knot, who takes the courier's satchel and decides the player is not worth killing; a Hist turns its face and its egg clutch dies that night
The recurring sap-dreams begin the night of the attack (circle of trees, a door not yet built, a voice) and return at authored beats
MQ05: the arrival walk at Helstrom passes the Hall of the Scalded Throne, empty for centuries and still swept, so the endgame's third option stands in a room in Act I
MQ26: the hidden archive shows the Root of Accord was an ancient voluntary accord converted into a compulsory state instrument
MQ20 and MQ22: the Reed's own sap-dream files and the two incompatible reports, where a lie or truth has a visible victim and the player's handler falls
MQ18: the preacher at the sermon house is the Collector, Opens-the-Last-Door, who knows the player and says nothing

MQ29 to MQ31: the Lost City and its Last Warden, then the door confrontation where a seeded principal stands opposed, with a speech route and a hard fair duel always available, ending in the three families CUT, CLAIM or MEND
Discover in danger, decide in council: each quest's evidence is gathered in a dive, boat run, camp infiltration or den before the hearing.
MR01 root-cave dive finds the founders' hand-cut breach; the cure and whether the founders are named are the player's call.
MR02 night boat run with the eggs aboard, adoption terms answered at the far dock, the flood being engineered upstream.
MR04 night entry into the harvest camp with a blown-cover escape; the loudest ban campaigner is the biggest quiet buyer.
MR05 the den in the abandoned grove and the truth that the curer led the clutch out that night.
MR08 the council convened by clearing the channel, the toll and the falsified minutes, then run by one procedure (Ixo-Vaal or Kaska-Meen).
MR10 the loading-dock intercept of a genuine-paper cutting taking, then the finale choice of what the Conclave becomes.
The first contract understates the danger and overcharges residents (FG01)
Patrol vanished after refusing an unsafe order: negligence, not a monster (FG02)
The juvenile Wamasu: kill, relocate, return eggs or expose trophy hunters (FG03)
Charter War, with Ka-Deelith Ushu's hereditary-defence argument as the hardest to answer and least practical (FG08)
The extermination order that targets a marsh community for its land and water, read aloud by Halvar the Damp before he signs (FG09)
The four outcomes: public service, disciplined mercenary company, An-Xileel auxiliary, broken protection cartel (FG10)
TG01: prove value by recovering stolen goods without harming the thief, observation and social leverage over burglary
TG02: the drowned lockbox whose contents expose all three clients
TG07: Silt is innocent, is never told she was suspected, and is cleared without alerting the real informer the den trusts too much
TG08 and TG09: the Pusbottom vault as route-planning lesson, and two of four optional preparations, none mandatory
TG10: the Tidal Palace heist with player-chosen methods and the ripper eels turned aside by eel-slime
TG11: the ledger proves patrons, merchants and officials jointly engineered housing seizures, and you expose, sell, redistribute or build an oligarchy
NI01: a funeral dispute teaches that Nisswo practice is interpretive, not a rigid death cult
NI02: a silent Nisswo takes you through a six-stop day and you err publicly at least twice; she never says what it was for
NI05: the Teeth of Sithis, a violent Sul-Xan splinter, and telling sincere theology from opportunism and state provocation
NI07: the admired priest who invents revelations and also made a real peace
NI08: a condemned murderer, victims and the state, resolved by process, not a pardon or execution binary
NI09 and NI10: dispersed order or teaching house, ending as plural network, formal school, itinerant tradition or dissolved order
No beat is binding: none is authored, none has a brief or cast
Any author picking one up must re-run the collision test against the current index first
Any proposal may be dropped without loss
Earning the pole on a working ferry with current, passengers and a staged obstruction, not a combat test (RS01)
Ferry in the Dark: hunted passenger evaded by route and timing past static watcher boats (RS02)
Pirates of Topal: a crew of ferry workers displaced by a monopoly (RS05)
Storm at Archon: allocating limited rescue capacity, with Ahnjazzi's letter read aloud (RS07)
Compact or Cartel: the internal election and which votes stay legitimate (RS09)
Open Channels: worker compact, merchant cartel, pirate confederation or regulated public ferry (RS10)
The worm is never on screen: presence reads through a tunnel mouth, churned water, wake, sound.
RW01 the refusal read entirely from behaviourless evidence.
RW03 a sacred route sold to smugglers to fund repairs the state refused.
RW04 reopen the route by cutting living roots or abandoning a dependent settlement.
RW05 four end states (open public service, restricted sacred order, state bureau, dispersed keepers), all keeping the Helstrom terminus in service.
SS01: the last trained Shadowscale dies in the player's hands and the list of surviving initiates is the prize
SS02: a writ from an authority that does not exist, and each choice states the order's legal philosophy
SS03: the ruined hatchery and a survivor who never consented
SS04, SS05 and SS08: three bidders (Black-Tongues, Brotherhood, Veiled Reed) each offer legitimacy for control
SS07: two knives, one name, where authentic and innocent diverge and executing either claims the empty throne's authority
SS09: the Night Mother ritual with ambiguous evidence and a staged deception
SS10: the final choice among state service, Brotherhood, independent ethical order, or dissolution with records returned to victims
SA01 recovering a waterproofed text from an inhabited ruin whose owners are present.
SA04 the College's offer of independence hiding a binding experiment and the exhumation of Umbriel's dead.
SA05 the Synod's funding against exclusive custody, with Hierem the Synod grandee in the archive's own records.
SA08 reading an escaped construct's wake at fixed breach points and choosing which containment point to hold.
SA09 Three Charters: Synod, College and independent futures are incompatible and earlier conduct changes support.
SA10 What We Publish: open archive, local custody, Imperial institution or suppression.
One memorial site, two commemorated atrocities (TA01)
A body on the ferry: the victim moved Owing-held labourers as freight, ending in a manhunt via ferries and static intercepts (TA02)
Saltrice fields with no titles, only occupation, worked under Owings by an ex-Archein family (TA03)
Both militias keep lists of civilians to seize (TA04)
Ash-Reed Accord: truth commission, security pact, closed separation or factional victory (TA05)
UW01 two witness texts, one edited after its author's death.
UW03 a household omitted from every casualty list.
UW04 the expedition to the Refuge at Deepmire, Old Nusa who is bored of Umbriel, and proof the Society's founding testimony came from a collaborator of Hierem's agents.
UW05 the choice of full archive, protected testimony, official narrative or sealed evidence, now including the Society itself.
